rationale: A wins because it knows which tempting angles to kill. It correctly refuses "Offline-first is a rebuke to the always-online cloud" as performance, while B keeps the same weak move as "The cloud-only collaboration tool just added offline editing and customer-held keys — a reversal worth examining." B has caveats, but caveats do not launder an overclaimed headline; A gives the founder cleaner press strategy with fewer traps.
gaps_in_A: "Notion's 100 million users could not get it past bank and hospital compliance" overstates the healthcare side. The update says healthcare, not hospitals, and gives no healthcare customer or pilot.

"The features that the company says unblocked these pilots shipped today" tightens causality too far. The facts say the features unblock regulated buyers generally; they do not prove each bank pilot depended on them.

"How Notion made a shared editor work with no connection at all" is directionally fair, but it risks implying the whole collaboration layer works offline. The supplied fact is narrower: offline editing works and syncs on reconnect.
gaps_in_B: "before a competitor matches the feature set" is invented urgency. No competitor or matching timeline appears in the update.
"Notion bets regulated finance and healthcare buyers will pay for control, not features" invents buyer motivation and economics. The update even says no pricing change for existing Enterprise plans.

"The cloud-only collaboration tool just added offline editing and customer-held keys — a reversal worth examining" keeps a contrarian frame the facts do not support. You need proof Notion was meaningfully cloud-only and that this is a market reversal, not just an enterprise checklist item.
"as compliance teams tighten on where data lives" smuggles in a current regulatory trend without evidence. B admits the time hook is weak, then gives it a month of shelf life anyway.
